speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia, along with a significant medical history. To begin our assessment, could you please describe the specific nature of your gait disturbances and when these symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing your symptoms; it sounds like you are experiencing significant coordination issues, particularly on the right side. To help narrow down the cause of this ataxia, have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs, and do you have a history of conditions like multiple sclerosis or vitamin deficiencies?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The combination of subacute limb ataxia and your history of natalizumab use for Crohn's disease is highly suggestive of PML, a rare opportunistic infection of the central nervous system. We need to confirm this immediately with imaging.

REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI_with_contrast
REQUEST TEST: CSF_analysis_for_JC_virus
